## Top Contenders

For a new Next.js SaaS in 2026, the right authentication pick is almost always Better Auth or Supabase Auth.

**Better Auth**
Better Auth is a modern, open-source authentication library built for full-stack TypeScript applications that stands out with its comprehensive feature set and plugin architecture. It offers the most complete feature set — 2FA, passkeys, RBAC, impersonation, and more — with no vendor lock-in and full self-hosting capabilities.

**Clerk**
Clerk is a hosted authentication service where you add their SDK to get production-quality sign-in screens and user management out of the box, paying per monthly active user — it is the fastest path to a working sign-in form and the slowest to scale a cost-controlled business on top of.

**Auth.js (formerly NextAuth)**

**Supabase Auth**
Supabase Auth is part of the larger Supabase platform, providing authentication alongside a PostgreSQL database, storage, and real-time subscriptions, with good Next.js integration through its JavaScript client library.

**Lucia**
Lucia is excellent at session management with secure defaults and works with any database, but "complete control" means 3-5x more implementation work than Auth.js for similar functionality.

## Key Takeaway

For anyone starting a new Next.js project, the choice is effectively between Better Auth and Clerk.

# Admin Plugin Setup & Usage

## Server-Side Auth Configuration

```ts
import { betterAuth } from "better-auth"
import { admin } from "better-auth/plugins"

export const auth = betterAuth({
    plugins: [
        admin()
    ]
})
```

## Client-Side Admin Client Setup

```ts
import { createAuthClient } from "better-auth/client"
import { adminClient } from "better-auth/client/plugins"

export const authClient = createAuthClient({
    plugins: [
        adminClient()
    ]
})
```

## Server-Side User Listing

```ts
const users = await auth.api.listUsers({
    query: {
        searchValue: "some name",
        searchField: "name",
        searchOperator: "contains",
        limit: 100,
        offset: 0,
        sortBy: "name",
        sortDirection: "desc",
        filterField: "email",
        filterValue: "hello@example.com",
        filterOperator: "eq"
    },
    headers: await headers(),
});
```

## Return Shape for `listUsers`

```ts
{
  users: User[],          // Array of user objects
  total: number,          // Total matching users
  limit: number,          // Limit parameter
  offset: number          // Offset parameter
}
```

## Generate Command

The `generate` command creates the schema required by Better Auth. If you're using a database adapter like Prisma or Drizzle, this command will generate the right schema for your ORM. If you're using the built-in Kysely adapter, it will generate an SQL file you can run directly on your database.

The syntax is: `npx @better-auth/cli generate`

## Migrate Command

The migrate command applies the Better Auth schema directly to your database. This is available if you're using the built-in Kysely adapter. For other adapters, you'll need to apply the schema using your ORM's migration tool.

The syntax is: `npx @better-auth/cli migrate`

## SQLite Specific Notes

For SQLite with Bun runtime, use bunx with the --bun flag to run cli commands to prevent seeing type errors related to recognizing the bun:sqlite module, eg: `bunx --bun auth@latest generate`

**Auth.js/NextAuth** — as of Sept 2025 it's officially in security-patch-only mode (Better Auth's team took over maintenance and recommends against starting new projects with it).
**Clerk/WorkOS** — hosted, per-MAU pricing, fastest but vendor lock-in and a paid dependency for what's currently a scaffold app.
**Better Auth** — actively developed, TypeScript-native, self-hosted, no vendor lock-in, first-class Next.js App Router support, built-in email+password and Google OAuth.

Going with **Better Auth** + SQLite (via `better-sqlite3`, zero external service). Implementing now.

## Why This Error Occurred

You are using the `middleware` file convention, which is deprecated and has been renamed to [`proxy`](/docs/app/api-reference/file-conventions/proxy).

## Migration to Proxy
